> **Synthetic data, software check only.** CMS DE-SynPUF
> (`bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop`) verifies that cohort SQL compiles to GoogleSQL, that
> it executes, and that data copied into DuckDB matches BigQuery. It says nothing about clinical performance or
> epidemiology, and SynPUF has no labs or vitals.

**Modes.** The default (`live: false`) needs no credentials and no network: it compiles the SQL and checks it.
`quarto render bigquery_duckdb_roundtrip.qmd -P live:true -P billing_project:<your-gcp-project>` runs the live
sections. Authenticate once, interactively, with `bigrquery::bq_auth()`. Never paste keys into this file; the
billing project is an id, not a secret.

```{r setup}
#| include: false
src <- Sys.getenv("OMOPDUCKDB_SRC")  # set to a checkout to test unreleased code
if (nzchar(src)) pkgload::load_all(src, quiet = TRUE) else library(omopduckdb)

billing <- Reduce(function(a, b) if (nzchar(a)) a else b,
  list(params$billing_project, Sys.getenv("OMOP_BQ_BILLING_PROJECT"),
       as.character(tryCatch(omopduckdb:::read_local_config("bigquery.yml")$billing_project, error = function(e) NULL))[1]))
if (is.na(billing) || identical(billing, "REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_GCP_PROJECT_ID")) billing <- ""
live <- isTRUE(params$live) && nzchar(billing)
if (isTRUE(params$live) && !nzchar(billing)) warning("live = TRUE but no billing project found; running offline.")
dataset <- "bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop"
out_dir <- tempfile("bq_demo_")
cat("mode:", if (live) "LIVE (BigQuery)" else "offline (no BigQuery calls)", "\n")
```

## 1. Offline checks (always run)

### 1a. Cohort and feature SQL are produced

A dry run compiles the diabetes phenotype to GoogleSQL and writes the feature queries. A placeholder project id is
used offline because nothing is sent to BigQuery.

```{r dry-run}
dry <- run_bigquery_demo(billing_project = if (nzchar(billing)) billing else "example-project",
                         output_dir = out_dir, dry_run = TRUE)
files <- list.files(out_dir)
files
stopifnot("features.googlesql.sql" %in% files, "availability.googlesql.sql" %in% files)
if (!"cohort.googlesql.sql" %in% files)
  message("CirceR/Java not available: cohort SQL not compiled (install CirceR to cover this step).")
```

### 1b. The SQL is GoogleSQL, not leftover T-SQL/DuckDB

Cheap static guards that catch dialect regressions without a BigQuery connection.

```{r dialect-guards}
sql <- vapply(list.files(out_dir, "[.]sql$", full.names = TRUE),
              function(f) paste(readLines(f, warn = FALSE), collapse = " "), "")
bad <- c(tsql_top = "SELECT[[:space:]]+TOP[[:space:]]", tsql_dateadd = "DATEADD[[:space:]]*[(]",
         tsql_hash = "#[[:alnum:]_]+", duckdb_interval = "INTERVAL[[:space:]]+'[0-9]+",
         unresolved_params = "@[[:alnum:]_]+")
hits <- vapply(bad, function(p) any(grepl(p, sql, ignore.case = TRUE)), NA)
data.frame(pattern = names(bad), found = hits)
stopifnot(!any(hits))
```

### 1c. DuckDB side of the shared CDM contract

The same OMOP tables BigQuery serves must exist in the local DuckDB schema, with the same columns. This is the
contract that keeps the two backends interchangeable.

```{r duckdb-contract}
cdm_db <- tempfile(fileext = ".duckdb")
invisible(capture.output(build_schema(cdm_db)))
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), cdm_db)
demo_tables <- c("person", "observation_period", "visit_occurrence", "condition_occurrence", "drug_exposure",
                 "measurement", "concept_ancestor")
ddl_types <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, sprintf(
  "SELECT table_name, column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name IN (%s)",
  paste0("'", demo_tables, "'", collapse = ", ")))
key_ids <- ddl_types[omopduckdb:::.is_key_id(ddl_types$column_name), ]
table(key_ids$data_type)
stopifnot(all(key_ids$data_type == "BIGINT"))  # 64-bit, like BigQuery INT64
```

### 1d. DuckDB demo on a small CDM, ids above 2^53 kept exact

`run_duckdb_demo()` builds the same cohort (native Circe compiler) and features (`inst/sql/duckdb_demo_features.sql`,
the DuckDB twin of the GoogleSQL template) that the BigQuery demo builds. The person id below is 2^53 + 1, which a
double cannot hold.

```{r duckdb-demo}
big_id <- "9007199254740993"
invisible(DBI::dbExecute(con, paste0("INSERT INTO person (person_id, gender_concept_id, year_of_birth, race_concept_id, ",
                           "ethnicity_concept_id) VALUES (", big_id, ", 8507, 1950, 8527, 0)")))
invisible(DBI::dbExecute(con, paste0("INSERT INTO observation_period VALUES (1, ", big_id, ", DATE '2016-01-01', DATE '2022-12-31', 0)")))
invisible(DBI::dbExecute(con, paste0("INSERT INTO condition_occurrence (condition_occurrence_id, person_id, condition_concept_id, ",
                           "condition_start_date, condition_type_concept_id) VALUES (1, ", big_id, ", 201820, DATE '2019-03-01', 0)")))
invisible(DBI::dbExecute(con, "INSERT INTO concept_ancestor VALUES (201820, 201820, 0, 0)"))
local_demo <- run_duckdb_demo(con)
local_demo$features
stopifnot(identical(local_demo$features$subject_id, big_id), nrow(check_id_precision(local_demo$features)) == 0)
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
```

### 1e. R and Python write the same BigQuery SQL

The feature and availability queries come from the same templates in both languages; the cohort SQL differs by design
(R: CirceR + SqlRender, Python: native compiler + sqlglot), which is why the live section compares their results.

```{r py-dry-run}
# the first Python that has the package (set OMOP_PYTHON to choose one); a bare python3 on the PATH often does not
py_ok <- function(p, mods) nzchar(p) && system2(p, c("-c", shQuote(paste("import", mods))), stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE) == 0
py_candidates <- unique(c(Sys.getenv("OMOP_PYTHON"), unname(Sys.which(c("python3", "python")))))
py <- Find(function(p) py_ok(p, "omop_etl.demo_bigquery, sqlglot"), py_candidates[nzchar(py_candidates)])
has_py <- !is.null(py)
if (has_py) {
  py_out <- tempfile("bq_demo_py_")
  system2(py, c("-m", "omop_etl.demo_bigquery", "--dry-run", "--billing-project",
                if (nzchar(billing)) billing else "example-project", "--output-dir", py_out), stdout = FALSE)
  same <- vapply(c("features.googlesql.sql", "availability.googlesql.sql"), function(f)
    identical(readLines(file.path(out_dir, f)), readLines(file.path(py_out, f))), NA)
  print(same)
  stopifnot(all(same))
} else message("Python package omop_etl (with sqlglot) not importable: skipped.")
# the live R vs Python check (4d) also needs the BigQuery client and application-default credentials
has_py_bq <- has_py && py_ok(py, "google.cloud.bigquery, db_dtypes")
```

The offline check that the *cohort* GoogleSQL keeps its meaning is in `tests/test_backend_parity.py`: it runs the
statements sent to BigQuery on DuckDB (transpiled back with sqlglot) and compares them with `run_duckdb_demo()` on a CDM
that exercises every step of the definition.

## 2. Live: BigQuery side

```{r live-run}
#| eval: !expr live
res <- run_bigquery_demo(billing_project = billing, output_dir = out_dir, dry_run = FALSE)
str(res[c("run", "n_cohort")], max.level = 2)
stopifnot(res$n_cohort > 0)
```

Utilization features and lab availability (SynPUF should report no numeric lab values):

```{r live-features}
#| eval: !expr live
res$clinical_telemetry
```

## 3. Live: BigQuery -> DuckDB copy and parity

Copies small tables into a throwaway DuckDB file and compares them with BigQuery: row counts, key ranges and a
column checksum. Large tables (`condition_occurrence`, `drug_exposure`, `concept_relationship`) are deliberately not
copied here because `load_from_bigquery()` holds a table in memory.

```{r live-copy}
#| eval: !expr live
db <- tempfile(fileext = ".duckdb")
load_from_bigquery(billing_project = billing, dataset = dataset, tables = params$load_tables, db_path = db)
# integer64: a 32-bit read turns large values (SUM(year_of_birth) on SynPUF is about 4.5e9) into NA
bq <- function(sql) as.data.frame(bigrquery::bq_table_download(bigrquery::bq_project_query(billing, sql), bigint = "integer64"))
dk <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), db, read_only = TRUE)

probe <- list(
  person = "SELECT COUNT(*) n, MIN(person_id) min_id, MAX(person_id) max_id, SUM(year_of_birth) sum_yob FROM %s",
  observation_period = "SELECT COUNT(*) n, MIN(observation_period_start_date) min_start,
                        MAX(observation_period_end_date) max_end FROM %s")
cmp <- do.call(rbind, lapply(intersect(names(probe), params$load_tables), function(t) {
  b <- bq(sprintf(probe[[t]], sprintf("`%s`.%s", dataset, t)))
  d <- DBI::dbGetQuery(dk, sprintf(probe[[t]], t))
  data.frame(table = t, metric = names(b),
             bigquery = vapply(b, function(x) format(x[[1]]), ""),
             duckdb = vapply(d, function(x) format(x[[1]]), ""))
}))
cmp$match <- cmp$bigquery == cmp$duckdb
cmp
stopifnot(all(cmp$match))
DBI::dbDisconnect(dk, shutdown = TRUE)
```

## 4. Live: same cohort, same features, same types

A fixed sample of persons (`MOD(person_id, 1000) = 0`, about 0.1%) is copied whole into DuckDB with
`copy_demo_sample_from_bigquery()`, with the `concept_ancestor` rows their events need. The cohort and the features
are per person, so rebuilding them on the copy must give exactly the BigQuery `demo_cohort` and `demo_features` rows
for the same persons. Each copy query scans its source table once; BigQuery bills the columns read, not the sample size.
SynPUF has no `visit_occurrence` or `measurement` table: the BigQuery demo used empty stand-ins for them (section 2's
report lists them), and the DuckDB copy keeps them empty too, so prior utilization is 0 on both sides and only the
cohort, demographics and types say anything.

```{r live-sample}
#| eval: !expr live
scratch <- paste0(billing, ".omop_duckdb_demo")
bq64 <- function(sql) as.data.frame(bigrquery::bq_table_download(bigrquery::bq_project_query(billing, sql, quiet = TRUE),
                                                                 bigint = "integer64", quiet = TRUE))
sample_db <- tempfile(fileext = ".duckdb")
copied <- copy_demo_sample_from_bigquery(billing, dataset, sample_db, sample_modulus = 1000L)
copied
sk <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), sample_db)
duck <- run_duckdb_demo(sk)
```

### 4a. Same Circe cohort

BigQuery's cohort came from CirceR + SqlRender (GoogleSQL); DuckDB's from the native compiler.

```{r live-cohort}
#| eval: !expr live
bq_cohort <- bq64(sprintf("SELECT * FROM `%s.demo_cohort` WHERE MOD(subject_id, 1000) = 0", scratch))
cohort_cmp <- compare_cohorts(bq_cohort, duck$cohort, examples = 5L)  # synthetic ids, safe to show
str(cohort_cmp)
stopifnot(cohort_cmp$match, cohort_cmp$n_left_rows > 0)
```

### 4b. Same features

```{r live-features-parity}
#| eval: !expr live
bq_feats <- bq64(sprintf("SELECT * FROM `%s.demo_features` WHERE MOD(subject_id, 1000) = 0", scratch))
feat_cmp <- compare_features(bq_feats, duck$features)
do.call(rbind, lapply(feat_cmp$columns, as.data.frame))
stopifnot(feat_cmp$match)
```

### 4c. Same column types, ids not truncated

BigQuery `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS` against the copied DuckDB tables and against the package's DDL. `only_*` rows
are columns of one CDM version only (SynPUF predates CDM 5.4) and are listed, not failed.

```{r live-types}
#| eval: !expr live
parts <- strsplit(dataset, ".", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
bq_types <- bq64(sprintf("SELECT table_name, column_name, data_type FROM `%s.%s.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS` WHERE table_name IN (%s)",
                         parts[[1]], parts[[2]], paste0("'", demo_tables, "'", collapse = ", ")))
copy_types <- DBI::dbGetQuery(sk, "SELECT table_name, column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns")
vs_copy <- compare_column_types(bq_types, copy_types)
vs_ddl <- compare_column_types(bq_types, ddl_types)
table(vs_copy$status)
table(vs_ddl$status)
vs_ddl[!vs_ddl$status %in% c("ok", "only_bigquery", "only_duckdb"), ]
stopifnot(!any(vs_copy$status %in% c("id_narrowed", "type_mismatch")),
          !any(vs_ddl$status == "id_narrowed"))
id_problems <- rbind(check_id_precision(bq_cohort), check_id_precision(bq_feats))
id_problems
stopifnot(nrow(id_problems) == 0)
max_ids <- bq64(sprintf("SELECT MAX(person_id) AS max_id FROM `%s.person` WHERE MOD(person_id, 1000) = 0", dataset))
stopifnot(identical(as.character(max_ids$max_id),
                    DBI::dbGetQuery(sk, "SELECT CAST(MAX(person_id) AS VARCHAR) AS m FROM person")$m))
DBI::dbDisconnect(sk, shutdown = TRUE)
```

### 4d. R and Python agree

Runs `python -m omop_etl.demo_bigquery` into its own scratch dataset (so it does not overwrite R's tables) and compares
its `demo_summary.json` and `demo_features.csv` with R's from section 2. It needs the Python BigQuery extra (`pip install "omop-duck-db[bigquery]"`,
which includes `db-dtypes`) and application-default credentials (`gcloud auth application-default login`); the R token is not shared with Python.

```{r live-python-skipped}
#| eval: !expr live && !has_py_bq
message("Skipped: Python with omop_etl, sqlglot, google-cloud-bigquery and db-dtypes is not available.")
```

```{r live-python}
#| eval: !expr live && has_py_bq
py_live <- tempfile("bq_demo_py_live_")
status <- system2(py, c("-m", "omop_etl.demo_bigquery", "--billing-project", billing, "--output-dir", py_live,
                        "--scratch-dataset", paste0(billing, ".omop_duckdb_demo_py")))
stopifnot(status == 0)
rp <- compare_demo_outputs(out_dir, py_live)
rp$summary_differences
str(rp$features[c("n_left", "n_right", "n_both", "match")])
stopifnot(rp$match)
```

## 5. Status of the checks

| Check | What it proves | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Same Circe cohort on DuckDB vs BigQuery `demo_cohort`: equal (subject, start, end) rows | Dialect translation preserves cohort semantics | Offline: `tests/test_backend_parity.py` (GoogleSQL emulated on DuckDB). Live: 4a |
| Feature parity: DuckDB feature extraction vs `demo_features` on the same persons | Utilization features agree across backends | Offline: same test, plus a hand-checked person. Live: 4b |
| Column-type parity (`INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS` vs DuckDB) incl. `INT64` -> `integer64` for ids | No silent id truncation | Offline: 1c, 1d and the tests (ids above 2^31 and 2^53). Live: 4c |
| Python path: `python -m omop_etl.demo_bigquery` output vs R `demo_summary.json` | R and Python agree | Offline: 1e and `test_r_and_python_duckdb_demo_agree`. Live: 4d |
| Vocabulary refresh: `sync_vocabulary_from_bigquery()` row counts vs source | Large-table streaming path | TODO (large, run manually) |
| Cost guard: `dry_run` bytes processed per query under a threshold | Demo stays cheap | TODO |
